label: Allied Telesis AT-x530-52GPXm
description: Allied Telesis AT-x530-52GPXm stackable L3 PoE+ switch: 40x 10/100/1000T PoE+ RJ-45, 8x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G PoE+ RJ-45 (48 PoE+ ports, 740 W), 4x 1/10G SFP+ uplinks, 240 Gbps switching fabric, 179 Mpps.

poe.note: 740 W from two fixed 370 W supplies - not 48 x 30 W. The vendor budget table gives 48 ports at 15.4 W PoE but only 24 ports at 30 W PoE+, and the installation guide states the same ceiling as "up to 24 Class 4 powered devices at 25.5 W". Every one of the 48 copper ports is a 30 W-capable IEEE 802.3af/at PSE port, so the per-port figure modelled is 30 W and the 740 W budget is what stops a full 30 W fill at 24 ports: 48 x 30 W would need 1440 W.

fabric.note: Vendor switching-fabric figure (forwarding rate 179 Mpps), the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates: 2 x (120000 Mbit/s of line rate).

notes: All 48 copper ports are PSE ports (40 gigabit ports 1-40 plus 8 multi-gigabit ports 41-48); the four SFP+ cages 49-52 are not. 441 x 421 x 44 mm, 6.9 kg, 88 W with no PoE load, 970 W fully loaded, 42 dBA. The 5.4.8-2 stand-alone installation guide carried its multi-gigabit limitation note only for the 28-port chassis (ports 21-24); no equivalent note for ports 41-48 was found in the guides checked here, so the current datasheet figure of 100M/1/2.5/5G is what is modelled. Console is the front-panel RJ-45 RS-232 port (AlliedWare Plus default 9600 8-N-1, no flow control; the switch ships with the manager/friend logins), reached with the RJ-45-to-DB-9 cable in the box or an AT-VT-Kit3 USB-to-serial cable. The management panel also carries a USB port and the eco-friendly button; neither is a network interface, so neither is modelled. Numbers: the x530 Series datasheet SPECIFICATIONS and Power and Noise tables and the model page at https://www.alliedtelesis.com/us/en/products/switches/x530-series; port numbering from the x530 Quick Installation Guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/file/2022-03/ati-x530-english-qig.pdf) and, for the 10/18/28GSX/DP port fronts, the VCStack installation guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/documents/installation-guides/ati_x530_vc_stacking_ig.pdf).
